# `Regex`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Regex — RE2 regex helpers.

Patterns use RE2 syntax (no backreferences, linear-time matching).
A pattern is compiled ONCE with `compile`, which turns an
invalid pattern into a typed `Err` — never a silent no-match.  Every
operation then takes the compiled, opaque `Regex`, so an invalid pattern
can never reach a match/find/replace/split as a false negative.

The `Regex` type is a built-in opaque handle (backed by
`ipe_runtime::regex_kernel::Regex`); it needs no explicit import.

Every operation caps the subject at a declared byte ceiling (default 16 MiB,
overridable via `IPE_REGEX_MAX_INPUT_BYTES`): a subject past the bound is
turned back at the boundary — `match` yields `False`, `find` `Nothing`,
`findAll` `[]`, `replace` the subject unchanged, `split` the subject as a
single element — so an untrusted subject can never drive unbounded work.
The ceiling is fixed when `compile` builds the `Regex`; a value that is not a
positive decimal byte count (`0` included) makes `compile` return `Err`.

## `compile`

```ipe
compile : String -> Result Error Regex
```

`compile pattern` — parse `pattern` into a reusable `Regex`.  An invalid
pattern is an `Err`, so the failure is observable at the call site rather
than silently degrading a later match.

## `match`

```ipe
match : Regex -> String -> Bool
```

`match re s` — does the compiled pattern match anywhere in `s`?

## `find`

```ipe
find : Regex -> String -> Maybe String
```

`find re s` — first match (Nothing if no match).

## `findAll`

```ipe
findAll : Regex -> String -> List String
```

`findAll re s` — every non-overlapping match in order.

## `replace`

```ipe
replace : Regex -> String -> String -> String
```

`replace re replacement s` — replace every match with `replacement`.
`replacement` may reference capture groups via `$1`, `$2`, etc. (RE2
substitution syntax).

## `split`

```ipe
split : Regex -> String -> List String
```

`split re s` — split on every match.
